context: Issue #44 tracks this bug. TASK-V031-WINDOWS-LIFECYCLE-ACCEPTANCE proved that published v0.3.1 itself, the stable checkout, and the Crew-owned DSH profile are correctly isolated, but the first real install was BLOCKED when the local profile-link step delegated to DSH/pnpm and pnpm returned ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION for 16 fresh @aws-sdk lockfile entries. Diagnose the exact Crew-owned profile/runtime shape and implement the minimal semantically correct policy-preserving registration path. Do not blindly edit profile metadata if that would leave required runtime dependencies or loader state invalid; prove the resulting registration is actually loadable/usable within Crew-owned state. A read-only `pnpm config get minimumReleaseAge` probe is allowed, but do not read unrelated global config or secrets. Preflight machine state from the prior run was DSH Crew plugin linked to the stable checkout, Codex integration not installed, Claude integration not installed; Claude CLI is present. The stable checkout is D:/Users/48376/Desktop/dsh-crew. Because this is a product installer fix after public v0.3.1, prepare version 0.3.2 consistently but DO NOT publish/tag/release it in this task.

editing or deleting the user's global pnpm config files

pnpm-lock.yaml unless a deterministic version-only preparation genuinely requires it; dependency updates are not authorized
official ~/.dsh, official web profile, official DSH credential/config stores, or unrelated user files
--purge or deletion of retained Crew config/backups
npm publish, dist-tag mutation, unpublish/deprecate, or any registry write
git tag creation/deletion/retargeting, GitHub Release mutation, branch rewrite, force-push, merge, rebase, or cherry-pick
runtime/routing/model-policy feature changes unrelated to installer/profile registration
secrets, tokens, credentials, cookies, API keys, or OTP output
